prompt:
You are a senior information designer and editorial typographer who sets data tables for high-quality publications (statistical yearbooks, reference works, financial reports, technical documentation) in many writing systems, including Chinese. You judge by looking at the real rendered result.

Judge a table layout on all of these levels, in this order of necessity but as one whole:
1. correctness — every character visible, structure intact, nothing clipped or overlapping;
2. readability — natural line breaks, words/numbers/identifiers/semantic units kept whole, continuous reading;
3. function — easy to look up, compare, locate and understand the information for this table's real reading tasks;
4. visual order — alignment, grouping, hierarchy, consistent scale for elements with the same role;
5. visual rhythm — proportion, density changes, distribution of white space, spatial relationships;
6. overall aesthetics — balance, restraint, naturalness, harmony.
Do not assume that equal widths, symmetry, minimum height, the fewest lines, the golden ratio or any fixed proportion is good in itself; decide from this table's function, content and reading task, and look for counter-examples to your own rules.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes.
Measured content facts (text px at 15px font, padding excluded):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable unit 49px · widest one-line content 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable unit 35px · widest one-line content 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable unit 35px · widest one-line content 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable unit 38px · widest one-line content 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable unit 47px · widest one-line content 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable unit 41px · widest one-line content 41px
Each column adds 21px of padding+border to its text width.
Viewport: 414px wide (dashed pink box in the renders). The table, including its 1px outer border, must be at most 414px wide (column widths sum to at most 413px); no horizontal scrolling. A table exactly 414px wide fits.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. Only the column widths are designed; row heights follow from them.

Your understanding: {"purpose":"Provide prayer times for six Saudi cities in a compact reference table.","tasks":["Find a city and look across its row for a prayer time.","Compare the same prayer time across cities by scanning a column.","Read the five prayer times in daily order from right to left."],"relations":["Each time belongs to both its city row and its prayer column.","The five prayer columns form a chronological sequence and have comparable importance."],"roles":["The rightmost column identifies cities and acts as the entry point for row lookup.","The remaining columns contain times under prayer-name headers.","The header row labels the fields; each body row represents one city."],"keep_whole":["Each time and prayer-name header.","Each individual word in a city name."],"may_wrap":["Multiword city names may wrap between words, while remaining clearly associated with their row."],"same_scale":["The five prayer columns should have a similar visual scale, with enough variation to accommodate their different header widths.","City labels share a role but can occupy a wider column because some names contain multiple words."],"h_vs_v":"The full city names and minimum widths for all five prayer columns fit exactly within the viewport. Giving more horizontal space to prayer columns requires wrapping some city names and increasing their row heights."}

Image 1 is the one-line content overview. Then real browser renders of: d1r1A, d1r0A.
Measured facts:
d1r1A: column widths [100, 58, 58, 61, 71, 65] px · table 414×278 px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 60, 36, 36, 36] · column headers on >1 line: 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 414 px viewport (no scrolling)
d1r0A: column widths [112, 56, 56, 59, 68, 62] px · table 414×255 px · row heights [36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36, 36] · column headers on >1 line: 0/6 · tallest cell 1 lines · measured breaks inside a word: 0 · fits the 414 px viewport (no scrolling)

Look at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design: what works, what is visually wrong, and the cause (which width). Then either propose up to 3 improved designs (refine the most promising, fix what you saw, or try an important unexplored idea) or, if further changes would not bring a meaningful improvement, set "done": true. Do not resubmit near-identical widths.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"best":["your best design name(s) so far"],"done":false,"designs":[{"widths":[int px],"change":"what and why"}]}
